label: Claude Haiku 5.5
output:
Last week (5–7 November) we ran the Winter School on Elliptic Curves and Modular Forms at the Department of Mathematics, Sahyadri Institute of Science, Pune. I was one of the three student organisers, so on behalf of the team, I want to say thank you.

Some numbers for those who like them: we received 112 applications and selected 41 participants (MSc and early PhD students) from 9 states, based on a statement and one reference each. A Rs 2.4 lakh grant from the institute's student initiative fund covered hostel stay and travel for 18 outstation students, so distance was not a barrier for anyone.

Thank you to our speakers. Dr. Nilesh Dharmadhikari (Hyderabad) took us through Mordell–Weil, Dr. Sunanda Iyer (Chennai) covered modular forms, and Dr. Tomasz Wierzbicki joined online from Kraków to walk us through computations in Sage. Thank you for making time for students.

To Prof. Anuradha Venkatesan, our faculty mentor: thank you for guiding us from the first planning meeting to the last day.

To my co-organisers Ketaki Joglekar and Faizan Mirza: this would not have happened without you.

Thanks to Mr. Prakash Salunke and the office staff. When the hostel bookings got messed up, he sorted out the rooms at 11 pm. Help like that doesn't show up in any programme, but it made a real difference.

Thanks also to the six PhD students who did the TA work. The problem sessions they ran worked well, and we plan to keep that format.

And to all 41 participants: you asked excellent questions, which is exactly what these schools are for. Small schools like this matter a lot for MSc students, because here you actually get to ask, not just sit at the back of a large hall.

Day 2 had its moment. The power went out for nearly two hours in the afternoon, laptops died, and we moved the problem session to the canteen with two rolling whiteboards. Honestly, it was the best session of the three days. One MSc student from Silchar also spotted an error in a worked example in Dr. Iyer's notes, she corrected it live, and she thanked him for catching it. That's what a good school looks like.

Slides and problem sheets will be uploaded to the department website within two weeks. We'll share the link here once it's up.

We hope to run a second edition in late 2027, provided we secure funding again. Watch this space.

Thank you, everyone.
